BiblicalUsage: To transplant is to plant again in better ground. God takes the highest branch of the high cedar and plants it upon a high mountain, the vine is planted in a good soil by great waters, and then is planted in the wilderness in a dry and thirsty ground. Jeremiah promises the man who trusts in the LORD shall be as a tree planted by the waters.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe transplanting is the story of every believer. God takes the tender branch and plants it where He chooses, and I hold that the tree by the waters does not fear the heat.
